headline: 50% on Canada went live Saturday and duration rallied — the first time this cycle the long end read a tariff as growth, not price.
stance: Section 338 duties of 50% on about $28bn of Canadian goods took effect 12:01am ET Saturday, overriding CUSMA origin, and Carney's answer is dated Sept 8. The bid this morning is in the 30y and in gold, with crude and Nasdaq futures lower — a growth read, and Wednesday tests it.

news.head: 50% Section 338 duties on Canada now in force
news.body: Live 12:01am ET Saturday on about $28bn of goods, and CUSMA origin does not exempt. Carney matches dollar-for-dollar from Sept 8 across six categories.

news.head: Bessent brings Iran sanctions to a podium today
news.body: Treasury holds a press conference this afternoon on what he has called the toughest sanctions in history. Brent $92.82, -1.7% (~6am ET) going in.

implications: Core PCE lands 8:30am Wednesday and Nvidia reports after that same close. One session carries the inflation print and the AI print, four days after the tariff and two before Warsh.
Retaliation with a Sept 8 date is scheduled damage, not priced damage. Two weeks of headline risk with a known end point is a hedging problem, not a positioning one.

watch.head: Bessent's Iran press conference, this afternoon
watch.body: Crude gave back 1.7% into it after two weekly gains above 5%. The announcement has been trailed for days; the scope is the only part not in the price.

watch.head: Core PCE, 8:30am ET Wednesday
watch.body: Forecast 0.3% on the core, with the Q2 GDP revision expected lower. Hot print plus soft revision is the pairing Warsh has to answer on Friday.

watch.head: Nvidia, Wednesday after the close
watch.body: Reports after Wednesday's close, the same session as core PCE. Nasdaq futures are taking that risk down two days early rather than on the day.

watch.head: Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, 10am ET Friday
watch.body: First symposium as chair, Aug 27-29. He walks in with a tariff shock four days old and no track record for the market to price him off.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 30y 5.24%, about 3bp below Friday's close (~6am ET). A 50% duty is a price-level shock and the long end bought duration anyway — that is a demand read, not a Fed read.
Section 338 overrides CUSMA origin. Every pass-through model built on treaty carve-outs is wrong by the size of the carve-out, and importers found out on a Saturday.
Gold $4,644/oz, +0.79% (~6am ET), bid alongside duration. Inflation compensation would have sold the long end this morning; a fiscal bid buys both, and it did.
sections.positioning: New this week: spec net long Swiss franc jumped ten points to the 88th %ile, the only fresh extreme in FX. That length went on before the Canada proclamation, not after it.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Nasdaq 100 futures -0.72% against S&P 500 -0.22% and Dow -0.09% (~3:40am ET). The trade shock is being expressed in AI multiples, not in trade-exposed industrials.
Canada's list is steel, dairy, appliances, ag equipment, pulp and electronics. Those names have a dated Sept 8 event, which is a rare thing to be able to hedge to.
sections.positioning: Spec net long S&P 500 futures came off five points to the 86th %ile last week, the first trim since the jump, and is still extended long into Wednesday's print.

single_name.note: Medifast — new to the screen today, insider buy filed Aug 21, above its 200-day. WW sits at the same score on the same list: two weight-management insiders in two sessions.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Friday's credit close was struck before the duties took effect Saturday. Today is the first mark on a tariff that is already law, so read last week's spreads as pre-event.
The duty hits importer working capital before any P&L. Fifty points on goods already on the water is a funding call, and it lands inside this quarter.
sections.positioning: Spec high-yield covered eight points to the 12th %ile last week, the largest move in credit. Extended short into a week carrying a tariff, a PCE print and Warsh.
